title: RuneScape Classic Stayed Online for 17 Years
hook: RuneScape's original 2001 version was still running until August 2018, long after bots had overrun it and Jagex's own tools stopped working on it. Did you ever log in to Classic before it closed?
script: Did you know the very first version of RuneScape stayed online for seventeen years before Jagex finally pulled the plug? RuneScape launched as a public beta on January fourth, 2001. In March 2004 it was replaced by RuneScape 2, and the old game was renamed RuneScape Classic. Jagex kept it alive on a small handful of servers. Classic was a magnet for cheaters, though. In August 2005 the free version was shut down because of widespread rule breaking. A few months later, only accounts that had logged in since that closure were allowed back in. Between 2009 and 2016 Jagex reopened Classic to members a few times for short windows. Then, on May twenty third, 2018, Jagex announced the end. Its modern tools for spotting bots and macros no longer worked with the old code. Botting kept growing, and some game breaking bugs could not be fixed. The servers went dark on August sixth, 2018, a little after nine in the morning UTC. Any leftover membership time carried over to RuneScape and Old School. Old School itself is built from a 2007 backup, so a piece of that era still lives on. Did you ever log in to Classic before it closed? Follow for more gaming history.
